newsitem.title: USA: Ill. University picks developer to plan expansion.
newsitem.headline: Ill. University picks developer to plan expansion.

text.p: University of Illinois at Chicago has selected a consortium of developers including Richard Stein to plan a campus expansion that could cost up to $400 million, a spokesman said Thursday.

A selection committee of university faculty, administration and staff members recommended a group including Mesirow Stein Real Estate Inc. as master developer to plan the expansion, spokesman Edward Tate said.

Selection of the group calling itself the South Campus Development Team LLC has been approved by Chancellor David Broski and must be approved by the university's board of trustees, which meets next in July, Tate said.

The consortium's agreement with the university includes an 18-month $731,000 contract to create the master plan for the expansion, which is to be built on land once occupied by the Maxwell Street market west of downtown Chicago.

The university's "wish list" includes a chemistry building, business school, office building, student housing and a performing arts center with conference space to meet its current and future needsd, Tate said.

University officials would also like to include residential development with some low-income housing and retail space in the expansion, Tate said. The expansion will also include a substantial park, he added.
Financing for the expansion will involve "a number of creative mechanisms," Tate said.
If all goes according to plan, groundbreaking for the first buildings in the expansion could be held in early 2000, Tate said.
The Stein-led group also includes New Frontier Cos. headed by William Cellini.
